case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the denial of a mother's motion to terminate a voluntary guardianship and remanded, holding the parent must first show by a preponderance that the impediments prompting the guardianship are gone, after which the non-parent bears a preponderance burden to overcome the parental presumption, a voluntarily created guardianship itself constituting exceptional circumstances that triggers best-interests review.
key_cases.relevance: Applies to families who voluntarily request a guardianship and later ask to have the child returned.
key_cases.quote: the natural parent must initially prove, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the impediments leading to the creation of the guardianship have been removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the order continuing a guardianship of a child and remanded, because the juvenile court applied a best-interests analysis without first expressly finding the exceptional circumstances required before a child is kept in a non-parent's custody.
key_cases.relevance: Arose from a parent's own request to the court to review the guardianship she had earlier agreed to.
key_cases.quote: The juvenile court's order does not expressly consider or mention exceptional circumstances.

key_cases.case_name: In the Matter of the Adoption of S.R.F.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a judgment terminating a mother's parental rights for abandonment under N.D.C.C. §§ 14-15-06(1)(a) and 14-15-19(3)(a) and granting the guardians' adoption petition, holding the abandonment findings were not clearly erroneous and overruling prior cases that had applied de novo review to adoption-act appeals.
key_cases.relevance: Begins with a mother voluntarily placing her child with family friends and consenting to their guardianship, the front-end self-referral route, and traces what happens when she does not follow through.
key_cases.quote: A party seeking termination of the parent-child relationship in the context of an adoption proceeding must prove the elements necessary to support termination by clear and convincing evidence.

state_agency.hotline: 1-833-958-3500 (8 a.m.-5 p.m. Central / 7 a.m.-4 p.m. Mountain, Mon-Fri; if a child is in immediate danger call 911)

mandatory_reporters: Listed professionals only — North Dakota is not a universal-reporting state (N.D. Cent. Code § 50-25.1-03(1))
Tier 1, 2, 3, and 4 mental health professionals (as defined in N.D. Cent. Code § 25-01-01) and any other medical or mental health professional
Religious practitioners of the healing arts
Schoolteachers, school administrators, and school counselors
Child care workers and child care licensors
Juvenile court personnel and probation officers
Licensed social workers and family service specialists
Members of the clergy, except when the knowledge is derived from information received as a spiritual adviser
Any person who discovers images of sexual conduct by a child on a workplace computer (N.D. Cent. Code § 50-25.1-03(3))
reporting_details: North Dakota is not a universal-reporting state: the professionals listed in N.D. Cent. Code § 50-25.1-03(1) must immediately report orally or in writing to the Department of Health and Human Services or its authorized agent, while any other person may report (N.D. Cent. Code §§ 50-25.1-03(2), 50-25.1-04(1)).

other: A child placed for care or adoption in violation of law

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately if there is a serious threat to the child's life or health; otherwise within department-set time frames

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: An extension of time must be requested of and granted by the department (N.D. Admin. Code § 75-03-19-04).
